Cyclic orbit search with Z17/Z34 acting on C^6 followed by staged symmetry release and LP polish.
direction: Symmetry-orbit constrained search followed by gradual symmetry breaking, exploiting $102=6\times17$: Let $\mathbb Z_{17}$ act on $\mathbb R^{12}=\mathbb C^6$ by multiplying the $b$-th complex coordinate pair by $\exp(2\pi i m_b/17)$ with distinct multipliers such as $m=(1,2,4,6,8,9)$; generate a full configuration from only six unit seed vectors, each producing a 17-point orbit, giving exactly 102 points with collisions rejected. Optimise the resulting 72-parameter problem with many random Adam restarts under an annealed soft-max objective, also trying the $3\times34$ analogue with $\mathbb Z_{34}$, then select the best symmetric code, unfold it to all 102 points, and progressively release the symmetry—first allowing orbit-common motions, then independent per-point Adam quench, and finally trust-region LP polish. If the optimum is structured rather than amorphous, this massively reduced search can find a basin invisible to perturbations of the jammed record; even if symmetry must ultimately be broken, the released configuration starts from a genuinely different contact topology.

idea: Escape the over-jammed basin with cheap subset-focused basin hopping — global kicks, random-subset re-randomization and worst-point best-hole reinsertion each quenched by fast annealed soft-max tangent descent without LPs, saving LP trust-region polish for the final seconds.

Frozen-core basin hopping that deletes/relocates blocks of 6-14 jammed points to create temporary slack, re-optimizes only the free block with annealed soft-max Adam against a fixed core then jointly, and wanders with Metropolis acceptance to rewire contact topology with almost no LP until a final snap.
Batched Riemannian Adam on softmax max-cosine over 16 diverse isotropic configurations with annealed sharpness and histogram-diversity elites, then short LP polish of only three distinct basins.
direction: Cheap batched from-scratch and isotropised population search without LP in the inner loop: Implement a batched Riemannian Adam minimising $\mathrm{softmax}_\alpha(\langle x_i,x_j\rangle)$ with $\alpha$ annealed from 20 to 250, operating simultaneously on $B=12$–20 configurations of shape $(B,102,12)$ via einsum so hundreds of restarts fit in $\sim$60–90 seconds. Seed the population diversely: pure random points, greedy farthest-point sphere samples, small perturbations of the record, and an isotropised record obtained by whitening so $X^\top X\approx(102/12)I$ followed by row renormalisation and iteration, since the incumbent's PCA projection is visibly anisotropic. Maintain elites by both score and permutation-invariant separation (sorted pairwise-cosine histograms) to avoid keeping copies of one basin, then give only the best three genuinely distinct elites an LP polish of at most 8 seconds each inside a 170-second cap. This tests whether an entirely different, more isotropic basin beats the record and eliminates the sparse-LP bottleneck responsible for the 200-second timeouts.

idea: Escape the over-jammed basin with Hessian soft-mode steps and rigid cluster rotations that preserve intra-cluster geometry, quenched by annealed soft-max descent.
direction: Coordinated soft-mode and rigid-cluster moves that preserve most contacts while rewiring the rest: Build the active contact graph using pairs within $2\times10^{-3}$ of the maximum, form the tangent-projected rigidity/Hessian matrix for a soft exponential pair potential (a $1122\times1122$ dense eigendecomposition is feasible once per cycle), and perturb the configuration along random combinations of its lowest 20–40 eigenvectors with amplitudes 0.02–0.15, rather than using coordinatewise noise. Alternate these spectral moves with cluster rotations: split points by sign of PC1 or by $k$-means into 4–6 clusters, rotate one cluster as a rigid body by 0.03–0.2 radians in a random coordinate 2-plane (preserving all intra-cluster cosines exactly), then quench with Adam and apply short LP only to candidates below 0.269. Track contact-graph edit distance and favour accepted intermediates whose score is within $\sim$0.002 of the incumbent but whose topology differs substantially, because escaping this jam requires collective motion along floppy directions, not stronger random shaking.

Target-feasibility cutting-plane search below the incumbent with slack-minimising trust-region LPs on the top violated pairs and a final min-max polish.
direction: Perform a target-feasibility cutting-plane search below the incumbent instead of repeatedly minimising the maximum from it: for targets $t=0.26718814-\delta$ with $\delta\in\{10^{-6},3\times10^{-6},10^{-5},3\times10^{-5}\}$, maintain only the currently most violated 200--500 pairs, and use sequential trust-region LPs that minimise the sum of nonnegative slacks $s_{ij}$ subject to the linearised constraints $\langle x_i,x_j\rangle+\langle u_i,x_j\rangle+\langle x_i,u_j\rangle\le t+s_{ij}$, tangent constraints, and $\|u_i\|_\infty\le r$; after each LP step renormalise, recompute the Gram matrix, replace the constraint set with the newly most violated pairs, decrease $r$ when total slack stalls and increase it after progress, and stop as soon as an actually feasible configuration with maximum below the incumbent is found, followed by one final ordinary LP polish under a strict 165-second internal deadline.

idea: Discrete symmetric pool plus greedy lexicographic selection and swap improvement followed by annealed descent and LP polish to reach a different basin.
direction: Search for a structurally different algebraic or lattice-derived basin by first constructing a large discrete candidate pool and solving the selection problem combinatorially: generate normalised D12-type roots with two coordinates equal to $\pm1/\sqrt2$, sampled three- and four-sparse sign vectors, coordinate vectors, and sampled vectors with entries in $\{0,\pm1/2,\pm\sqrt3/2\}$ patterns, giving at least 20,000 candidates; greedily build a 102-set by minimising first the maximum cosine, then the number of pairs within $10^{-4}$ of that maximum, then a soft-max penalty, improve it with many one-for-one swap moves from the pool under the same lexicographic objective, and only afterwards release the selected points into continuous annealed descent and LP polishing, thereby testing highly symmetric sparse configurations that perturbations of the current dense contact graph are unlikely ever to reach.

Iterated multi-point cavity reconstruction that deletes mutually-contacting overloaded clusters, spreads the remainder with annealed soft-max descent, and greedily reinserts points from 20k candidates with tangent refinement before a short LP snap.
direction: Use multi-point cavity reconstruction rather than single-point hole insertion: rank points by contact count and, if available, LP dual weight, delete $k\in\{4,6,8,12\}$ overloaded or mutually contacting points, reoptimise the remaining $102-k$ points with annealed soft-max descent and short LP polishing so that they actively spread into the vacated region, then reinsert the deleted points one at a time at the best of at least 20,000 random spherical candidates scored lexicographically by maximum cosine against the current set and number of near-maximal contacts, locally optimise each inserted point on its tangent space while holding the others fixed, and run only a short LP polish after all insertions; repeat with different deletion subsets and accept a trial only if its fully polished value beats the incumbent, while always retaining the incumbent as the returned fallback.

idea: Wander among basins with cheap row-normalized soft-max repulsion quenches, hole kill-reinsert and coordinated regional kicks, accepting slightly worse moves to change contact topology, with trust-region LP used only for final polish to avoid jamming and timeouts.

Evolve a diverse population of cheaply quenched optima from differently kicked and hole-reinserted copies of the record, then recombine pairs via assignment-matched Procrustes alignment and subset/slerp crossover with a final LP polish of the two best children.
direction: Build a small population of genuinely distinct local optima and recombine them: generate 8--16 incumbents using different random seeds, kick strengths, deletion fractions, and annealing schedules, polish each cheaply without the LP, fingerprint each by its sorted pair-cosine histogram and thresholded contact adjacency, and retain a diverse subset rather than only the lowest scorer. For pairs of retained optima, match points by solving a linear assignment problem on pairwise inner products, align them by orthogonal Procrustes/Kabsch rotation, construct children by taking matched point subsets from each parent or by normalized spherical interpolation for matched pairs, and then quench and LP-polish only the best two children by a fast soft-max screen; this explores unions of two contact topologies that local kicks around the single record cannot reach.

idea: Batched population search with continuation power repulsion and fingerprint diversity without intermediate LPs, final LP only.
direction: Run a genuinely batched population search with diversity preservation and no intermediate LP calls: evolve $B=24$ configurations simultaneously as a $(24,102,12)$ array, including random starts and differently scaled perturbations of the incumbent, using vectorised Riemannian Adam on the continuation objective $\sum_{i<j}((1+\langle x_i,x_j\rangle)/2)^p$ with $p$ increased through $4,8,16,32,64$, periodically compute pairwise basin fingerprints from sorted near-contact Gram values, discard or reinitialise duplicate basins while retaining distinct elites, and use the soft objective's best distinct configurations as the only candidates for LP polishing in the final 20 seconds; enforce time checks inside the batch loop and a hard return of the best verified configuration by about 165 seconds, avoiding both repeated single-trajectory basin hopping and uncontrolled LP time.

idea: Break the jammed contact graph with SVD nullspace slides targeted at NNLS stress contacts followed by log-sum-exp annealing and selective LP snapping.
direction: Use contact-Jacobian nullspace and LP-dual stress information to deliberately break the jammed contact graph: construct the Jacobian of pairs within $10^{-7}$ of the maximum, compute its leading near-null tangent directions by SVD, identify high-stress contacts from nonnegative least-squares equilibrium weights $w_{ij}$ satisfying the per-point balance conditions, and take comparatively large steps, of angular size roughly $0.03$--$0.15$, along combinations of near-null directions chosen to deactivate 20--80 selected high-stress contacts while monitoring newly approaching pairs. Follow each such slide with log-sum-exp continuation at temperatures decreasing from $0.01$ to $0.0005$, accept endpoints based on both objective and contact-graph distance from the incumbent rather than objective alone, and apply the expensive LP only to endpoints below about $0.2685$ or with at least 10% changed contacts.

idea: Delete overloaded clusters of 10-18 points, spread the remainder with annealed soft-max Adam to gain margin, then regrow one-by-one by 50k-sample global hole search with local refinement and full Adam re-optimization, accepting intermediate worsening before short LP snaps.
direction: Perform simultaneous many-point deletion and global regrowth rather than replacing one to three points: identify the 12 points with the largest contact counts and largest row-wise maxima, remove 10--18 of them, re-polish the remaining 84--92 points with annealed log-sum-exp descent so they develop a margin below $0.267$, and then reinsert the removed points one at a time using global hole search from at least 50,000 random sphere samples plus local spherical optimization against the fixed points, re-optimizing all points for 300--600 Adam steps after each insertion. Allow the intermediate 102-point objective to worsen to about $0.275$--$0.29$, run several deletion sets derived from different overloaded clusters, keep any configuration whose contact adjacency differs materially from the incumbent, and reserve only the final 20 seconds for LP polishing under a strict 165-second internal deadline.

idea: Escape the jammed basin by cluster-cavity reconstruction: delete a mutually-contacting overloaded neighborhood and greedily reinsert spread points in the created hole, then anneal with fast log-sum-exp repulsion, reserving expensive LP only for a final snap.

Delete 10-18 overloaded points, quench the remainder for margin, then regrow one-by-one with 50k-sample global hole search plus spherical refinement and Adam re-optimization, wandering to topologically distinct basins.
direction: Perform simultaneous many-point deletion and global regrowth rather than replacing one to three points: identify the 12 points with the largest contact counts and largest row-wise maxima, remove 10--18 of them, re-polish the remaining 84--92 points with annealed log-sum-exp descent so they develop a margin below $0.267$, and then reinsert the removed points one at a time using global hole search from at least 50,000 random sphere samples plus local spherical optimization against the fixed points, re-optimizing all points for 300--600 Adam steps after each insertion. Allow the intermediate 102-point objective to worsen to about $0.275$--$0.29$, run several deletion sets derived from different overloaded clusters, keep any configuration whose contact adjacency differs materially from the incumbent, and reserve only the final 20 seconds for LP polishing under a strict 165-second internal deadline.

idea: Escape the jammed basin with LP-free basin hopping — multi-hole deletion plus cluster kicks followed by fast annealed soft-max Adam, saving trust-region LP for one final snap to allow many topology changes without timeout.

Greedy construction from sparse signed pools with two-scale layering followed by joint scale/rotation plus Riemannian annealing to reach a new balanced basin, then final comparison against the record.
direction: Search from a structured algebraic construction completely independent of the record: generate a large pool of sparse signed candidate vectors in $\mathbb{R}^{12}$ with coordinate patterns such as permutations and signings of $(1,1,0,\ldots)$, $(1,1,1,1,0,\ldots)/2$, $(1,0,\ldots)$, and two-scale layered versions of these patterns, greedily select 102 candidates minimizing the current maximum inner product with randomized tie-breaking, and then continuously optimize a small number of layer scale/rotation parameters together with all point positions. Run several randomized greedy selections and template families in parallel sequence, use the best structured result as a new basin for annealed descent, and compare it against the record only at the end; even if its initial score is only $0.28$--$0.32$, its sparse, balanced contact topology provides a starting point structurally unlike the jammed incumbent.

idea: Wander with large cavity moves that delete an overloaded contact-cluster, let the remainder spread, greedily re-insert far holes, then annealed soft-max quench — using only cheap quenches in the loop and one short LP snap at the end to stay in time.
Break the jam with Jacobian nullspace slides targeted at NNLS stress contacts, quenched by log-sum-exp continuation and gated LP polish.
direction: Use contact-Jacobian nullspace and LP-dual stress information to deliberately break the jammed contact graph: construct the Jacobian of pairs within $10^{-7}$ of the maximum, compute its leading near-null tangent directions by SVD, identify high-stress contacts from nonnegative least-squares equilibrium weights $w_{ij}$ satisfying the per-point balance conditions, and take comparatively large steps, of angular size roughly $0.03$--$0.15$, along combinations of near-null directions chosen to deactivate 20--80 selected high-stress contacts while monitoring newly approaching pairs. Follow each such slide with log-sum-exp continuation at temperatures decreasing from $0.01$ to $0.0005$, accept endpoints based on both objective and contact-graph distance from the incumbent rather than objective alone, and apply the expensive LP only to endpoints below about $0.2685$ or with at least 10% changed contacts.
